clinician.final_diagnosis: Pulmonary Echinococcosis (Hydatid Cyst of the Left Lower Lobe)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 34-year-old Middle Eastern female with significant epidemiologic risk (family livestock-herding occupation in Middle East involving sheep and cattle exposure) presented to the emergency department with one month of excessive coughing, mild dyspnea, and left-sided chest pain. Initial CXR revealed a 10cm x 8cm opacity in the left lower lobe. CTA on hospital day 1 confirmed a hypodense abnormality with characteristic features of a simple pulmonary cyst. Initial laboratory work showed aminotransferase and alkaline phosphatase elevations. On hospital day 6, thoracic surgery was consulted due to repeat imaging and persistent clinical symptoms without significant change. Given the radiologic concern for risk of spillage with CT-guided aspiration, a complete left lower lobe lobectomy was performed for diagnostic evaluation. Post-surgical pathology of the clear cystic fluid confirmed Echinococcus with identification of hooklets characteristic of the parasite, despite similar morphologic appearance in other Taeniidae family members (including T. solium). Concurrent lymph node biopsy showed mild anthracosis and benign lymphoid hyperplasia without malignancy. Echinococcus antibody serology returned negative. The patient was discharged on Albendazole for treatment of both E. granulosus and E. multilocularis with serial follow-up CXR recommended for 10 years.
